title: Check: Similar Shapes: Area and Volume

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have areas of $8\text{ cm}^2$ and $50\text{ cm}^2$. What is the length scale factor from the smaller to the larger?
questions.explanation: The area ratio is $\frac{50}{8} = \frac{25}{4}$. The length scale factor is $\sqrt{\frac{25}{4}} = \frac{5}{2}$.

questions.stem: Two similar cylinders have volumes of $24\text{ cm}^3$ and $192\text{ cm}^3$. What is the ratio of their surface areas?
questions.explanation: The volume ratio is $\frac{192}{24} = 8$, so the length scale factor is $\sqrt[3]{8} = 2$. The surface area ratio is $2^2 = 4$, giving a ratio of $1 : 4$.

questions.stem: A model car is built at a scale of $1 : 10$. If the real car has a capacity (volume) of $5000\text{ litres}$, what is the capacity of the model?
questions.explanation: The length scale factor is $\frac{1}{10}$. Volume scales by the cube: $\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{1000}$. The model's capacity is $\frac{5000}{1000} = 5\text{ litres}$.
